description: Synthesis data for the agentic-sdlc-process-orchestrator category pack. category_pack.load_pack_overlay attaches it to the pack only when a need profile selects that pack; no other research uses it.
naming_rules: Use product-level names (e.g. Augment Cosmos not Augment Code; Devin not Cognition+Devin). Apply parent/child dedupe from pack aliases.
research_brief_lines: Multi-market landscape — chart + solution cards **per market**:
1. **Primary (APO):** Agentic Process Orchestrators — compliance wrappers above host runtimes.
2. **Secondary (SDLC plugins):** OSS methodology packs (BMAD, GSD, Superpowers, GitHub Spec Kit, Oh My plugins, Zuvo, SuperClaude, Ruflo) — substitutes for an APO even when adjacent to it.
3. **Tertiary (agentic SDLC SaaS):** Factory/Factory.ai, Devin, Augment Cosmos, Tembo — substitutes even when vendors do not self-label APO.
APO targeting must NOT exclude secondary-market OSS/plugin substitutes from solution cards or charts.
Apply the factory↔factory-ai aliases from the category pack.
Few products self-label APO; map Cosmos/Factory/Devin-class vendors as landscape peers per the market definition.
market_overview: Agentic SDLC orchestration sits **one level above coding agents**: process catalogs, gates, and specialist routing rather than raw codegen. Three markets are scored separately — **Agentic Process Orchestrators (APO)** (primary), **SDLC plugins & methodology packs** (secondary), and **agentic SDLC SaaS / autonomous delivery** (tertiary). Shortlist by market, not from a single blended ranking.
key_findings: Hook-enforced gates plus durable cross-session state are the scarce combination; methodology packs without them are skippable prompt/persona layers, so they are not placed as Leaders on that basis alone.

resolution_notes.subject: magic-dev
resolution_notes.decision: One membership: hard-excluded as `coding_agent` by the category pack. Not a SaaS core, comparison column, MQ/Wave point or Top Commercial card. Model seed lists that re-include it are envelope quotes, not report membership.

resolution_notes.subject: conductor
resolution_notes.claim: Conductor as APO peer vs aggregator
resolution_notes.decision: Aggregator (SaaS-adjacent coding-agent aggregator), not an Agentic Process Orchestrator; not plotted on the APO chart.

resolution_notes.subject: secondary-packs
resolution_notes.claim: Secondary packs lack gates/state, so they are empty or not worth buying
resolution_notes.decision: Secondary packs are host-plugin substitutes for plan-to-ship workflows. Leader demotion is specifically about missing hook gates and/or cross-session state, not a blanket claim that the pack is useless.
resolution_notes.evidence: sdlc-plugins core membership in catalog_audit / chart-data and matrix ticks.

problem_statement: Coding agents execute work; they do not by themselves **enforce** an SDLC. Buyers need a process layer so planning, verification, review, and release cannot be skipped when agents run in parallel or across sessions.
out_of_scope: Generic **coding agents** and IDE copilots (Cursor Background Agents, Cline, Aider, Continue, OpenHands, SWE-agent)
**Host runtimes** that execute code without a process catalog (Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code, Codex as hosts — listed under Adjacent)
**Single-step** tools (PR review bots, PM integrations such as Linear)
**Generic agent frameworks** without SDLC process packaging (LangGraph, CrewAI as adjacent)
**Sunset** products named in the pack's sunset registry
market_overview_lines: The category is **early mainstream**: buyers separate agent hosts from process layers, but few vendors combine machine-readable catalogs with hook-enforced gates.
Verify latest data — market size estimates for agentic SDLC orchestration are not web-verified in this synthesis.
- **Maturity**: executor-first agents are ahead of process catalogs.
- **Commercial vs OSS**: OSS frameworks dominate experimentation; commercial players lead managed execution.
- **SMB vs enterprise**: SMBs favour templates, predictable pricing, and managed hosting; enterprises prioritise audit, SSO, and residency.
- **Deployment**: SaaS agents, IDE plugins, and self-hosted OSS graphs coexist; switching costs rise with hook and catalog lock-in.

trend_seeds.title: Process-first orchestration above coding agents
trend_seeds.what: Buyers increasingly separate the agent host (IDE, cloud sandbox) from the SDLC process layer that composes workflows, enforces gates, and records skills.
trend_seeds.smb: SMBs without platform teams need opinionated process packs rather than bespoke agent graphs.
trend_seeds.vendor: Vendors that market explicit SDLC chains are listed in the per-market sections; executor-first hosts remain executor-first.

trend_seeds.title: Hook-enforced lifecycle gates
trend_seeds.what: Host hooks that fail closed on skill recording, planning ownership, and delivery gates are emerging as trust rails for autonomous work.
trend_seeds.smb: Reduces rework risk when junior teams delegate multi-step agent runs.
trend_seeds.vendor: See the Hook-enforced gates row of the matrix for who ships them.

trend_seeds.title: Machine-readable workflow catalogs
trend_seeds.what: Atomic flow catalogs (workflows, steps, V-loops) enable composition, audit, and CI freshness checks beyond ad-hoc prompts.
trend_seeds.smb: Lets lean teams adopt SDLC patterns without writing orchestration code.
trend_seeds.vendor: See the Atomic flow catalog row of the matrix.

trend_seeds.title: Git-native issue→PR agent loops
trend_seeds.what: Issue trackers and repos become control planes for multi-step agent work with human review on PRs.
trend_seeds.smb: Fits teams already on GitHub; lowers integration tax versus custom runtimes.
trend_seeds.vendor: Vendors targeting this pattern are those with CI integration in the matrix.

trend_seeds.title: Autonomous software engineers (plan→ship)
trend_seeds.what: Managed agents that plan, implement, test, and open PRs in customer repos are maturing for enterprise pilots.
trend_seeds.smb: High capability but opaque process; pricing and governance remain enterprise-weighted.

trend_seeds.title: BYO agent runtimes and graph orchestration
trend_seeds.what: Frameworks expose durable graphs, interrupts, and delegation primitives for custom orchestration.
trend_seeds.smb: Maximum flexibility at the cost of in-house agent ops expertise.
trend_seeds.vendor: Generic frameworks are adjacent unless they package an SDLC process.

trend_seeds.title: Spec-driven and context-engineering workflows
trend_seeds.what: Lightweight methodology packs emphasize intent specs, critique loops, and context hygiene before code.
trend_seeds.smb: Low-cost entry for teams not ready for full orchestration platforms.

trend_seeds.title: Multi-model pools and triangulated research
trend_seeds.what: This research pass triangulates multiple model families with explicit divergence tracking. That is a report method — not a product feature vendors were scored on.
trend_seeds.smb: Use triangulation to interrogate marketing claims; do not treat it as a matrix tick.
trend_seeds.vendor: Not a scored MQ/Wave/matrix axis in this engine; see scoring methodology.

adjacent_note_lines: Pack-specific adjacency calls (host runtimes, aggregators, CRM-style tools) are listed per vendor below with the pack's reason.
buying_guidance_lines: - **Host-runtime path**: Use a coding-agent host (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) with a separate process pack. The host is not the orchestrator.
- **Managed autonomous delivery**: Shortlist the agentic-sdlc-saas cores. This profile does not resolve to an OSS process pack.

outlook.title: Router-first catalogs and hook gates
outlook.what: Process routers with nested verify loops remain a differentiator for teams that need fail-closed delivery, not just prompt packs.

outlook.title: Consolidation of git-native agents
outlook.what: Issue-to-PR agents may merge with SDLC orchestration platforms.
outlook.smb: Threatens point tools without ecosystem depth.

consensus_themes.title: Process layer above host runtimes
consensus_themes.text: Contributing models treat Agentic Process Orchestrators as a process or enforcement layer above a host coding-agent runtime, not as a synonym for autonomous code generation.

consensus_themes.title: Hook-enforced and deterministic gates
consensus_themes.text: Models agree that machine-checkable gates (host hooks, blocking quality rails) are the main differentiator versus prompt- or persona-level methodology packs, which an agent can skip.

consensus_themes.title: SDLC plugin / methodology packs as substitutes
consensus_themes.text: Models agree the secondary market (BMAD, GSD, Superpowers, Spec Kit, Ruflo, Oh My Pi, and peers) covers plan-to-ship workflows as host plugins. That is a substitute class, not automatic Leader standing on the primary APO chart.

consensus_themes.title: Cross-session state is under-served
consensus_themes.text: Models agree durable cross-session state is the weakest inclusion criterion for most methodology packs; markdown re-read per session is not an enforced state machine.

consensus_themes.title: Tertiary SaaS as buying substitutes
consensus_themes.text: Models agree Factory.ai, Devin, and Augment Cosmos are analyst-grade substitutes for process-orchestration buying even when they do not self-label as APO. They are scored in the SaaS market, not as APO peers.
